## Task
Do A and B name the same business concept (the same real-world thing, so the classes model one concept under different names)? Concepts that merely share attributes such as an id or a date are not the same.

### A
concept: Booking
where: SessionService (uses), src/business/sessionService.ts, component business
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
const ticketsUsed = active.reduce((n, b) => n + b.tickets, 0);
=====SOURCE-END=====

### B
concept: Club Booking
where: ClubBookingRepository (uses), src/persistence/clubBookingRepository.ts, component persistence
code:
=====SOURCE-BEGIN
private readonly bookings = new Map<string, ClubBooking>();
=====SOURCE-END=====
graph:
- class ClubBookingRepository (node 440da90bcde7901a): layer infrastructure, component persistence, fan-out 0, fan-in 7

- <- CONSTRUCTOR_INJECTS Class ClubBookingService
- <- CONSTRUCTOR_INJECTS Class SessionService

response.rationale: These are two different concepts. A Booking is a per-session reservation that holds a ticket count. SessionService adds these up in `active.reduce((n, b) => n + b.tickets, 0)` and loads them through BookingRepository.findBySession. A Club Booking is a separate entity (`Map<string, ClubBooking>`) with its own repository and its own service (ClubBookingService), which offers create, get, list and invoice. SessionService looks Club Bookings up by date (ClubBookingRepository.findByDate) and uses them in effectiveCapacity, so they reduce the capacity a session has left rather than being bookings of a session. The two have separate repositories, services and lifecycles (Club Bookings are invoiced), so they are different real-world things, not one concept under two names.
